answer: No. Your records show lisinopril was stopped on September 22, 2025 because it gave you a dry cough, and Dr. Marsh switched you to losartan 50 mg daily. Your cough went away by the December 2025 visit. The app that still lists it is most likely working from an old copy: the only record that shows it as active is a hospital health-app export retrieved in March 2025, before the change. Lisinopril is also recorded as an intolerance (cough), and I found nothing showing it was ever restarted. Your current blood pressure medicines in the records are losartan, amlodipine 5 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg. Please don't take lisinopril and losartan together. I'd ask that app to remove lisinopril, and mention it to your doctor or pharmacist. One more thing to raise with your doctor: a March 2026 hospital record says hydrochlorothiazide was stopped for low sodium, but your clinic and your own May 2026 list still show it, and your sodium was still slightly low (134) in June 2026. They should confirm whether you should be on it.
short: Lisinopril was stopped on 22 Sept 2025 for a dry cough and replaced by losartan 50 mg; it should not be on my current list. Separately, please confirm whether hydrochlorothiazide should continue, since a March 2026 hospital record says it was stopped for low sodium.
